evidence.quote: the increase in contingent work over the past decade has coincided with an increase of one-third in the share of employees working part time but who would prefer to work full time

For monetary policy, the growth of contingent work affects the way we assess maximum employment and the way we interpret important labor market outcomes, such as the level of part-time employment and aggregate hours worked.
cyclical changes in resource utilization could be reflected less in movements in the unemployment rate and more in variation in hours per worker.
We are still at an early stage in these developments, and it is too soon to say how these changes will play out.

parsed.rationale: The speech is a structural discussion of gig and contingent work, and it offers no guidance on rates or inflation. Its mild emphasis on underemployment and hidden slack leans slightly dovish on the labor market, but there is no clear policy signal.
